around.headline: FDA seizes Rs 5 crore of spurious drugs carrying fake MNC labels near Bidadi
around.summary: Karnataka's drug-control authorities busted a racket manufacturing counterfeit medicines branded with genuine multinational company labels, seizing stock worth about Rs 5 crore near Bidadi. Buy medicines only from licensed pharmacies and check strip details rather than trusting the brand name printed on the packet.

around.headline: ORR firms ask GBA to defer Rs 450-crore white-topping work, push work-from-home instead
around.summary: The Outer Ring Road Companies Association has written to the Greater Bengaluru Authority opposing the white-topping project slated to start in October, arguing it will choke an already-congested corridor, and are floating a temporary WFH push as an alternative. If you commute along ORR, expect this timeline dispute to shape your daily traffic for months.
around.source: ThePrint, The Times of India, The Hindu

around.headline: Namma Metro Phase 2A trials expected from October; Silk Board flyover section still lagging
around.summary: Trial runs on the Metro's Phase 2A stretch are expected to begin in October, but the elevated section over the Silk Board flyover is behind schedule. Commuters banking on Metro as relief from ORR traffic should not expect that corridor open soon.

around.headline: Voter-roll revision raises risk of genuine Bengaluru voters being dropped from the list
around.summary: A report flags how genuine voters could inadvertently slip off the electoral rolls during the ongoing revision exercise. Worth checking your own entry on the CEO Karnataka portal now rather than discovering an issue on election day.

around.headline: Bengaluru's 15-lakh-sapling Guinness record bid cost the city Rs 12.5 crore
around.summary: Civic records show the tree-planting drive that won Bengaluru a Guinness World Record ran up a Rs 12.5-crore bill, prompting questions over the spending. Relevant if you track how BBMP/GBA civic budgets get allocated.

around.headline: Y Combinator sells another 1.2% stake in Bengaluru-based Groww for Rs 1,435 crore
around.summary: Early investor Y Combinator has trimmed its holding in fintech platform Groww further in a secondary sale worth Rs 1,435 crore. A sign of continued investor appetite for Bengaluru-headquartered startups even as the broader funding climate stays selective.

street_smart.title: You need to restart a chronic-condition medicine and a small pharmacy near your stop offers it at a noticeably lower price than the usual chemist, still in a sealed strip with a familiar MNC brand printed on it. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Today's report that Karnataka's FDA seized Rs 5 crore worth of spurious drugs carrying fake MNC labels near Bidadi (The Times of India).
street_smart.situation: The strip looks fine at a glance — foil intact, familiar brand name, a batch number printed on the back. The shop isn't one you recognise, and there's no visible pharmacist or registration certificate on the wall.

choices.text: Buy it — the packaging has the recognisable MNC brand printed on it, so it must be genuine.
choices.feedback: This is exactly the mechanism behind today's Bidadi seizure: the fake stock was deliberately printed with genuine multinational labels so it would pass a glance-level check. Brand printing on a strip proves nothing about where or how it was made — counterfeiters copy it precisely because buyers trust it.

choices.text: Buy it, but ask for a cash receipt so you have proof of purchase if something goes wrong.
choices.feedback: A receipt helps you get a refund later, but it does nothing to confirm the medicine itself is genuine, and by then you may have already taken a spurious drug — a real health risk for anything you're relying on to manage a chronic condition.

choices.text: Skip the discount, buy from a licensed pharmacy with a visible registration certificate and a pharmacist on duty, and check the batch number against the manufacturer's site or helpline if you're ever unsure.
choices.feedback: Correct. Licensed pharmacies source through verified supply chains and are legally accountable, which is the actual check that matters — not what's printed on the strip. Cross-checking a batch number directly with the manufacturer closes the gap that counterfeit labelling is designed to exploit.

choices.text: Post the shop's name on a local social media group as a warning before buying anything else.
choices.feedback: Public warnings can help others eventually, but posting unverified suspicion first can misfire — if the shop turns out legitimate you've damaged a real business, and if it isn't, a social post is far slower than reporting it to the drug control department, which can actually inspect and act.

takeaways: A genuine-looking brand name or logo on a strip is not proof of authenticity — counterfeiters print real MNC labels on purpose; buy medicines only from a licensed pharmacy with its registration certificate on display.
For chronic or high-value medication, you can call the manufacturer's toll-free number or check their website with the batch number if a source feels uncertain.
Report suspected spurious or fake drugs to the Karnataka Drugs Control Department rather than just avoiding the shop quietly — that's how seizures like today's Bidadi bust get triggered.

quiz.question: What did Karnataka's FDA seize near Bidadi today, worth around Rs 5 crore?
options: Spurious drugs carrying fake MNC labels
quiz.why: The racket printed genuine multinational company labels on fake medicine to make it pass casual inspection — brand printing alone isn't proof of authenticity.

quiz.question: The Outer Ring Road Companies Association has asked the GBA to defer which Rs 450-crore project, due to start in October?
quiz.why: The association argued the road work should wait until Metro service is running on the corridor, and floated a temporary work-from-home push as an interim alternative.

quiz.question: Bengaluru's 15-lakh-sapling Guinness World Record bid reportedly cost the city how much?
quiz.why: Rs 1,435 crore was actually the size of a separate, unrelated deal today — Y Combinator's secondary sale of a 1.2% stake in Bengaluru-based fintech Groww.

quiz.question: Bengaluru sits at roughly what elevation above sea level, one reason it doesn't sit directly on a major river like most big Indian cities?
quiz.why: The city's height means its Cauvery water supply has to be pumped nearly 100 km and lifted close to 500 metres in elevation — one of the largest such pumping systems in the country.

quiz.question: The Outer Ring Road companies addressed their objection letter to which body, which has taken over several BBMP functions in Bengaluru?
quiz.why: The GBA was created to take over city governance and infrastructure functions that previously sat with the BBMP, which is why civic and infrastructure letters like this one now go to it.
